newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil hit by falling futures, easier prems.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil hit by falling futures, easier prems.

text.p: NWE gas oil was knocked lower by easier futures and slipping premiums which fell on the back of a surplus of prompt material.
Traders said activity was improved, particuarly for Russian and DIN grades for second half business.
March IPE gas oil closed $1.25 a tonne weaker at $164.75 after a session of choppy trade and thin volumes.
Traders said most attention was focused on second half March, with some people anticipating opportunities to take NWE material out of region.
Asian spring refinery maintenance was seen giving support to second half March gas oil as was anticipation of the next Indian tender.
"The second half is seeing a lot of business on top of the two 77,000 tonne cargoes done earlier in the week," said one trader.
Heating oil barge premiums were pressured $1 lower with talk centered around March IPE flat to +$1 fob on early March, but there were few takers.

Russian premiums were down $1 or so to March IPE flat with two 40,000 tonne cargoes heard done at flat March cif NWE for very early March. A smaller 10,000 tonne parcel was able to attract March IPE +$1.25 cif, the higher price reflecting size and discharge port.

FOD activity was slow although a 20,000 tonne cargo was sold today at March flat cif NWE, off up to $3, for an early March delivery. Second half March material was heard offerred at March IPE +$2.50/3.00.
A Scandinavian 20,000 tonne heating oil cargo was also heard sold into Poland at cif high quotes +$3.50.

DIN premiums were weaker with premiums down to March IPE flat. A small 10,000 tonne piece was done at March IPE +$3 cif Rostock, the price reflecting the size and port. A second cargo into Hamburg, in addition to yesterday's was understood done at March IPE +25 cents.
"DIN has tumbled recently, it was only a couple of weeks ago that it was taking +$8," said one trader.
Diesel bucked the general trend for weaker premiums. Traders said a 20,000 tonne cargo sold at March IPE +$15 cif NWE for March 8-12 dates.
